title: Weekly TP stability sync notes (Serving Runtime) — 2025
content:
Working doc — keep it lightweight / practical. Not a replacement for Confluence design/ADR. This is the weekly pulse + decisions + who’s doing what.

Standing meeting: Weekly TP Stability Sync (30–45m)
Cadence: Tue 10:30–11:15 PT (occasionally ad hoc during incidents)
Chair: Talia Benson (PgM)
Tech lead: Noah Patel

Goals (reminder)
- Stop TP hangs/timeouts under sustained mixed load (prefill+decode, long context, bursty concurrency)
- Add detection/diagnostics: compute vs comms vs scheduler
- Add regression coverage (repro harness + perf canary)
- Add safe mitigations: watchdog + abort/drain + runbooks/alerts

Quick links
- Initiative: ENG-4821 (umbrella)
- Design doc (Confluence): TP stability fixes (kernel + scheduling)
- ADR: adr-0127-tp-watchdog-and-abort-semantics
- Known issues page: tensor-parallel-hangs-under-load
- Slack threads: 1739784412, 1739812205, 1739897721, 1739973309, 1740071202, 1740165551

============================================================
Week of 2025-02-11 — Kickoff + repro focus
Attendees: Noah, Hiro, Sofia, Rina, Marcus, Omar, Rafael, Aisha, Talia

Top of mind
- Current symptoms in Dedicated A100 80GB clusters: request hang -> downstream timeouts; looks like decode step stalls and never recovers.
- Unclear if primary root cause is scheduler starvation vs NCCL ordering mismatch vs cancellation path (client disconnect).

Status
1) Repro harness (ENG-4822)
- Rina: close to first reliable repro in benchmark-lab w/ mixed prompt lengths + streaming decode.
- Hypothesis: long prefill batches cause decode ranks to diverge / starve collectives.
- Next: lock down seed + distributions so we can run it in perf-canary.

2) Instrumentation (ENG-4823)
- Omar/Julian: draft metric names for per-rank heartbeat + stall reason enums.
- SRE request: labels must be low-cardinality; need replica_id + rank (rank bounded by TP=2/4/8).

3) Scheduling (ENG-4824)
- Sofia/Lena: investigating fairness/ordering guardrail: ensure that when a TP group enters “collective region” all ranks make progress (no rank allowed to run ahead into next op).
- Concern: perf regression if we over-synchronize.

4) NCCL stream/event ordering (ENG-4825)
- Hiro/Grace: code pointers identified. There are multiple code paths: graph-captured decode vs non-captured; stream semantics differ.
- Action: write down expected ordering contract (what events must be waited on and where).

Blockers
- Need one canonical hang signature with logs/trace so we’re not mixing multiple issues.

Decisions
- Define “primary repro target” as: mixed prefill+decode + streaming enabled + bursty concurrency; aim for hang within <30 min under load.

Action items
- Rina: publish “repro recipe v0” in benchmark-lab (commands + config + expected symptoms). Due 2025-02-14.
- Omar: propose metric names + initial stall reason codes in Slack thread 1739897721. Due 2025-02-13.
- Sofia: write 1-page note describing suspected starvation mechanism + where to instrument scheduler. Due 2025-02-14.

============================================================
Week of 2025-02-18 — Sev1 follow-ups + tighten scope
Context: 2025-02-17 Sev1 Dedicated timeouts suspected TP hang (Slack 1740165551)
Attendees: Noah, Hiro, Sofia, Sean, Rafael, Aisha, Tomáš, Connor, Talia (+ ad hoc Grace/Omar)

What happened (short recap)
- Multiple Dedicated replicas (TP=4) started timing out; draining replicas improved but didn’t eliminate recurrence.
- Detection gap: we paged on customer-facing timeouts, not on early stall signals. No clear “comms stuck” vs “compute stuck.”

Status
1) Incident artifacts
- SRE: postmortem draft started (Confluence postmortems/2025-02-17-tp-decode-hang-sev1)
- Tomáš: runbook gap list captured in eng-oncall thread 1740169022.

2) Instrumentation PR underway
- PR: redwood/pr-21834 (TP heartbeat metrics + stall reason codes)
  - Adds: per-rank heartbeat timestamp, in-flight collective counter gauge, scheduler queue depth, and structured log line on stall detection.
  - Open questions: default stall threshold vs model size; avoid paging on false positives.

3) Repro
- Slack 1739784412: first successful repro on A100 80GB with mixed workload. Still not fully deterministic but trending.
- Repro signature: rank 2 stuck waiting on stream event prior to NCCL all-reduce; other ranks advance until they block.

4) NCCL ordering
- Slack 1739812205: suspected mismatch; we likely have “collective called on different stream ordering” under certain cancellation or graph capture boundary.

Blockers / risks
- We may have multiple bugs: (a) starvation causing delayed collective entry, (b) missing stream/event sync, (c) cancellation path leaving collectives half-entered.

Decisions
- Split deliverables into 3 “must ship” fixes for runtime 1.19:
  A) Instrumentation + dashboard/alert hooks (heartbeat + stall reason)
  B) NCCL stream/event sync hardening in collective boundary
  C) Watchdog + safe abort/drain semantics (feature-flagged)
- Scheduler fairness change will proceed but be gated carefully (risk of perf regression).

Action items
- Connor: create release planning ticket ENG-4829 and propose canary order (Dedicated first). Due 2025-02-19.
- Hiro/Grace: draft PR for NCCL sync hardening (ENG-4825). Due 2025-02-21.
- Rafael/Aisha: define alert thresholds & routing policy (Slack 1740071202). Due 2025-02-22.
- Tomáš: start runbook v0 (runtime-tp-hang-mitigation). Due 2025-02-24.

============================================================
Week of 2025-02-25 — Implementation sprint: PRs landing + rollout planning
Attendees: Noah, Hiro, Sofia, Marcus, Rina, Omar, Rafael, Aisha, Sergio, Connor, Talia

Status (by workstream)

A) Instrumentation / observability
- PR merged (or near-merge): redwood/pr-21834
  - Notes: use stall_reason enum values in logs (compute_busy, comms_wait, scheduler_starvation, kv_compaction, unknown)
  - Follow-up PR: redwood/pr-21872 adds NCCL collective counters to tracing spans.
- Observability pack:
  - observability-pack/pr-412 adds dashboard panels + initial alert rules (heartbeat gaps, stall reason counts, timeout correlation).

B) Scheduler fairness / collective starvation guardrail
- PR: redwood/pr-21841 (scheduler guardrail)
  - Sofia notes: prevents prefill-heavy batches from indefinitely starving decode collectives; introduces explicit “collective gate” checkpoints.
  - Perf: microbench shows small overhead in light load; mixed load improvement in p99 (less stall amplification) but needs broader perf-canary confirmation.
  - Risk: potential throughput regression under uniform short prompts.

C) NCCL stream/event sync hardening
- PR: redwood/pr-21853
  - Adds explicit cudaEventRecord/Wait around collective boundaries; conditional behavior under CUDA graph capture.
  - Slack 1740251033: microbench results show ~0.3–1.2% overhead in decode-only; mixed workload noisier; want feature-flag or environment toggle.

D) Watchdog + safe abort/drain
- PR: redwood/pr-21860
  - Adds watchdog timers for TP step duration; on trigger -> structured error, drain replica, surface error code to routing.
  - Defaults: OFF behind flag “tp_watchdog_enabled” (need final naming).
  - Slack 1739973309: debate about default timeouts; plan is model-size-based with progressive rollout.
- PR: redwood/pr-21912 improves NCCL error surfacing to API layer (actionable error codes).

E) KV cache + compaction interaction
- PR: redwood/pr-21866
  - Fixes a rank divergence edge-case when compaction triggers mid-decode; adds stress coverage.

F) Repro + regression
- benchmark-lab: pr-97 adds mixed workload repro harness config.
- perf-canary: pr-188 adds TP long-context stress scenarios + thresholds.
- Marcus: drafting additional stress scenarios (bursty concurrency, replica churn) for ENG-4828.

Blockers
- Need a single “go/no-go dashboard” for canary (SRE wants a checklist + must-pass metrics).
- Need to agree on rollback triggers (hang rate vs timeout rate vs watchdog triggers vs drain events).

Decisions
- Canary gating metrics (initial proposal):
  - TP heartbeat gap rate: < 1 / 10k requests per cluster-hour (warn), < 1 / 50k (pass)
  - Request timeouts attributed to runtime: reduce by 80% vs baseline on canary clusters
  - Watchdog triggers: expected low but non-zero; if > 1 / 1k req or correlated to false positives -> disable flag
  - Drain events: dedupe + rate-limit alerts to avoid paging storms

Action items
- Sergio/Aisha: publish “TP stall + timeout dashboard v0” with panel list + owner mapping. Due 2025-02-27.
- Connor: write canary schedule proposal (which Dedicated accounts/clusters, who on point). Due 2025-02-27.
- Noah: finalize stall taxonomy mapping to mitigation guidance (what to do for comms_wait vs scheduler_starvation, etc.). Due 2025-02-28.
- Marcus/Rina: confirm perf-canary thresholds & run frequency for TP stress scenarios. Due 2025-02-28.

============================================================
Week of 2025-03-04 — Canary readiness + alert noise reduction
Attendees: Noah, Hiro, Sofia, Rafael, Aisha, Tomáš, Sergio, Connor, Talia (+ Omar, Marcus)

Status
- Release planning: ENG-4829 in progress; target runtime 1.19 canary window mid-week (Dedicated first).
- Feature flags:
  - tp_watchdog_enabled (default OFF) — will be enabled only on canary clusters initially.
  - tp_nccl_sync_hardening (TBD naming) — likely default ON, with rollback if perf regression.
  - scheduler_collective_guardrail (default ON for canary only pending perf).

Key updates
- Alert noise: PR redwood/pr-21921 dedupes replica drain events + rate-limits certain stall alerts.
- Load shedding: PR redwood/pr-21875 wires stall signals into overload protection so new requests are rejected/redirected rather than piling onto a wedged replica.
- Cancellation path bugfix: PR redwood/pr-21890 fixes deadlock on cancelled streaming requests in TP (client disconnect).
- Safer defaults: PR redwood/pr-21897 adjusts concurrency caps for TP (feature-flagged) as a mitigation while rollout proceeds.

Operational readiness
- INT-2219 filed to enable extra NCCL debug logging during canary window (time-boxed). Ensure security/perf review.
- Runbook v0 drafted by Tomáš; needs quick review for “exact commands to run” + “where to look first” (SRE asks for copy/paste).

Open questions
- Watchdog thresholds by model size: need a table (or heuristic). Concern about long-context models triggering false positives.
- For watchdog-triggered abort: do we always drain replica vs attempt in-process recovery? Current approach: drain. ADR supports drain.

Decisions
- Canary plan: start with 2 Dedicated clusters with known issues (A100 80GB TP=4) + 1 “clean” cluster as control.
- Paging policy: page only on correlated increases in customer timeouts OR sustained heartbeat gaps; do not page on single watchdog trigger.

Action items
- Rafael/Tomáš: finalize on-call runbook steps + escalation checklist and link it from alerts. Due 2025-03-05.
- Aisha/Sergio: confirm alert thresholds in 1740071202 thread and update dashboard doc. Due 2025-03-05.
- Hiro: provide final perf numbers (decode-only and mixed) for NCCL sync hardening; include GPU types tested. Due 2025-03-06.
- Sofia: perf-canary comparison for scheduler guardrail (baseline vs canary) and recommendation (ON/OFF default). Due 2025-03-06.
- Connor: send go/no-go checklist to eng-releases thread 1740401120. Due 2025-03-06.

============================================================
Parking lot (carryover topics)
- Need a “stall signature catalog” with example logs/traces for each stall_reason (Omar). Useful for Support/SRE.
- KV cache compaction + TP: want more coverage under memory pressure (Samir/Marcus).
- Longer-term: consider health-checking NCCL communicator state and preemptively draining when comms_wait persists.

Notes to self (Talia)
- Keep initiative ENG-4821 updated w/ clear milestone dates and explicit owners.
- Make sure PM ticket PM-911 stays aligned (Dedicated customer comms, esp. Acme AI).
- Ensure postmortem action items are all linked (no orphaned tasks).
